claims.claim: Chevron reported earnings of $12.1 billion for the second quarter of 2026.
Second quarter 2026 reported earnings were up from $2.5 billion in the same period last year.
Adjusted earnings were $12.0 billion.
Return on capital employed was 21 percent.
Foreign currency effects decreased earnings by $49 million.
Cash flow from operations was $22.6 billion.
Cash flow from operations in the second quarter of 2025 was $8.6 billion.
U.S. upstream earnings were $3.5 billion.
U.S. upstream earnings were up from $1.4 billion in the second quarter of 2025.
The increase in U.S. upstream earnings was driven by higher liquids realizations and sales volumes.
International upstream earnings were $4.6 billion.
International upstream earnings were up from $1.3 billion in the second quarter of 2025.
The increase in international upstream earnings was due to higher sales volumes and liquids realizations.
U.S. downstream earnings were $2.4 billion.
U.S. downstream earnings were up from $404 million in the second quarter of 2025.
The increase in U.S. downstream earnings was primarily due to higher margins on refined product sales.
International downstream earnings were $2.5 billion.
International downstream earnings were up from a loss of $1.0 billion in the second quarter of 2025.
claims.note: Wrong period and wrong sign. International downstream earned $333 million in 2Q 2025; the $(1,013) million loss is the 1Q 2026 column.

claims.claim: The increase in international downstream earnings was due to higher margins on refined product sales and favorable timing effects.
No specific guidance was provided for future periods.
Capital expenditures were $4.5 billion for the quarter.
Capital expenditures were up from $3.7 billion in the second quarter of 2025.
Total debt was reduced by $8.4 billion in the quarter.
Total debt stood at $37.1 billion following the reduction.
Foreign currency effects decreased earnings by $49 million in the quarter (restated in Watch Items).
